name: Sol
description: A middle-aged yellow dwarf and its court of eight planets, three named dwarf worlds, two debris belts, and a retinue of comets. Four and a half billion years of accretion, migration, and bombardment settled into the most thoroughly charted system known. Every ephemeris in the sector ultimately answers to the clocks kept here.

stars.name: Sol
stars.description: A steady G-class dwarf fusing hydrogen into helium at fifteen million degrees in its core. Its eleven-year activity cycle drives space weather across all eight planets, and its wind sculpts the heliosphere far past the Kuiper belt. Total output has risen thirty percent since the planets formed, and will keep rising.

planets.name: Mercury
planets.description: A scorched iron-hearted rock racing around the Sun in eighty-eight days, its cratered face swinging between furnace days and frozen nights. Tidal locking history left it with a slow fifty-nine-day spin and a strangely oversized core. Missions brave the thermal extremes for the water ice hiding in permanently shadowed polar craters.

planets.name: Venus
planets.description: A cloud-wrapped furnace where ninety-two bars of carbon dioxide drive a runaway greenhouse to four hundred sixty-four degrees. Its surface, young by crater count, repaved itself in planet-wide volcanic floods within the last billion years. Retrograde spin and crushing pressure make landers brief heroic footnotes.

planets.name: Earth
planets.description: The only confirmed living world, its blue oceans and oxygen air the product of four billion years of biology. A large moon steadies its tilt while plate tectonics recycle the crust and regulate the climate. Every survey crew in history launched from here, and all of them file it as home.

moons.name: Moon
moons.description: A quarter-million miles of battered highland keeping tidal lock with Earth since the giant impact that made it. Its phases pace calendars while its gravity brakes the homeworld's spin century by century. Footprints from the first landings still lie undisturbed in the regolith.

planets.name: Mars
planets.description: A rust-red desert of extinct volcanoes and dry riverbeds, crowned by polar caps of water and carbon-dioxide ice. Olympus Mons rises three Everests while Valles Marineris would span a continent on Earth. Robotic outposts multiply yearly, and every crew manifest argues about who goes first.

moons.name: Phobos
moons.description: A lumpy captured rock spiraling inward a few meters per century toward eventual breakup into a ring. The Stickney crater dominates one face, nearly the wound that would have shattered it. Its regolith is the cheapest reaction mass in the inner system.

moons.name: Deimos
moons.description: A smooth dust-mantled pebble in a slow high orbit, one of the smallest known moons. It drifts outward almost imperceptibly while its sibling falls inward. Relay stations favor it for its quiet sky and gentle station-keeping.

planets.name: Jupiter
planets.description: A banded giant eleven times Earth's width, its Great Red Spot a storm wider than worlds that has raged for centuries. The magnetosphere dwarfs the Sun itself and traps radiation belts lethal to unshielded hulls. Its gravity shepherds the asteroid belt and flings comets out of the inner system.

moons.name: Io (Jupiter I)
moons.description: The most volcanic body known, resurfaced constantly by sulfur eruptions from tidal kneading. Plumes rise hundreds of kilometers while lava lakes glow through fractured crust. Any lander would melt, corrode, and be irradiated in that order.

moons.name: Europa
moons.description: A bright cracked ice shell hiding a salty ocean with twice Earth's water beneath. Lineae fracture patterns record tides that may keep the deep sea warm and chemically rich. It tops every list of places to look for living things.

moons.name: Ganymede
moons.description: The largest moon in the system, bigger than Mercury, with its own magnetic field and buried ocean. Grooved terrain mixes ancient dark ground with younger bright ice. Its aurorae rock back and forth with the parent magnetosphere.

moons.name: Callisto
moons.description: The most cratered surface anywhere, four billion years of impacts preserved in ice. Valhalla basin's rings span thousands of kilometers from an ancient cataclysm. Its dead calm makes it the preferred radiation shelter of the outer system.

planets.name: Saturn
planets.description: The ringed jewel, its broad icy bands spanning hundreds of thousands of kilometers yet only meters thick. Average density runs lower than water, and hexagon storms circle the north pole. Shepherd moons sculpt the gaps while geysers on Enceladus feed the faint outer ring.

moons.name: Enceladus
moons.description: A brilliant snowball venting ocean spray through tiger-stripe fractures at its south pole. The plumes feed a diffuse ring and sample a salty sea kept liquid by tides. Flythroughs tasted organics, and every return mission is argued over fiercely.

moons.name: Titan
moons.description: A smog-shrouded giant moon with methane rain, rivers, and polar seas under orange haze. Dunes of organic sand circle the equator while cryovolcanoes may resurface the water-ice bedrock. It is the most Earthlike place nobody can breathe.

planets.name: Uranus
planets.description: An ice giant knocked on its side, rolling around the Sun at a ninety-eight-degree tilt. Methane paints it featureless teal while the coldest planetary atmosphere on record barely stirs. Its rings stand vertical like a target viewed edge-on.

planets.name: Neptune
planets.description: The windiest world, supersonic methane storms tearing through deep blue haze at two thousand kilometers per hour. Found by mathematics before any telescope, it guards the edge of the giant-planet realm. Its captured moon Triton orbits backward, a kidnapped dwarf planet.

moons.name: Triton
moons.description: A captured dwarf world circling backward, its nitrogen geysers erupting through pink ice. Cantilevered terrain suggests a subsurface ocean slowly freezing from the top down. Tidal decay will shatter it into a ring within a few billion years.

dwarfPlanets.name: Ceres
dwarfPlanets.description: The belt's largest resident, a rounded world of rock and ice brine between Mars and Jupiter. Bright salt deposits in Occator crater mark where briny water reached the surface. Prospectors value its water above its minerals.

dwarfPlanets.name: Pluto
dwarfPlanets.description: A heart-glaciered world of nitrogen ice and tholin haze, demoted but unforgotten. Sputnik Planitia's churning ice sheet renews itself while water-ice mountains stand kilometers tall. Its five-moon family, led by Charon, dances a complex gravitational ballet.

dwarfPlanets.name: Haumea
dwarfPlanets.description: A fast-spinning elongated egg, one revolution every four hours, ringed and double-mooned. A giant impact stripped its ice mantle and scattered a whole collisional family. Its strange shape makes every light curve a puzzle.

dwarfPlanets.name: Eris
dwarfPlanets.description: The massive scattered-disc world whose discovery forced the dwarf-planet reckoning. Nearly Pluto's size but far denser, with methane frost brightening its face. Its moon Dysnomia circles a world colder than any planet.

asteroids.name: Vesta
asteroids.description: A differentiated protoplanet with basalt lava flows and a south-polar basin nearly its own diameter. Fragments knocked loose fall to Earth as a distinct meteorite clan. Dawn's mapping made it the best-understood rock in the belt.

asteroids.name: Pallas
asteroids.description: A tilted carbon-rich worldlet on a highly inclined belt orbit. Its surface holds hydrated minerals prized by volatile prospectors. The inclination makes rendezvous expensive and its charts correspondingly thin.

belts.name: Main Belt
belts.description: A torus of a million rocky fragments between Mars and Jupiter, ground down over eons. Jupiter's resonances carved the Kirkwood gaps and still stir the lanes. Miners work the M-types while surveyors catalog the rest.

belts.name: Kuiper Belt
belts.description: A vast icy disk beyond Neptune holding dwarf worlds, binaries, and short-period comet reservoirs. Resonant plutinos keep time with Neptune while the scattered disc drifts outward. Cold classicals here preserve the system's formation chemistry.

comets.name: Encke
comets.description: A short-period regular returning every three years on a torrid inner orbit. Its dust feeds the Taurid meteor showers each autumn. Devolatilized crust makes it fainter every apparition.

comets.name: Halley
comets.description: The famous retrograde visitor, recorded since antiquity and returning every seventy-five years. Its dark nucleus erupts in jets as sunlight reaches buried ice each perihelion. The next return is already circled on a billion calendars.

comets.name: Hale-Bopp
comets.description: The great comet of the nineties, its thirty-kilometer nucleus visible to the naked eye for eighteen months. Sodium tails and twin dust streams made it the most observed comet in history. Now outbound past fifty AU, it sleeps until the year four thousand.
